survey: A pair of orange flip-flops lying side by side on a teal striped background, seen from above at an angle, toe ends toward the lower left. Each has a flat sole with a dotted grip area at the toe end. A yellow toe post rises from that grip area. A Y/V-shaped yellow strap goes back from the post, and its two ends go into slots in the sole near the heel half. Both soles lie flat and cast soft shadows, so nothing floats. The two sandals point the same way and are almost identical copies of each other.

errors.where: Yellow straps on both flip-flops, at the inner (left) strap arm and its slot
errors.what: The strap ends are not anchored on both side edges of the sole. One arm swings out past the sole's left edge and curls back into a slot near the middle of the sole, beside the other arm's slot. The strap makes a closed hook rather than a V that spans the foot, so a foot could not slide in and the sandal could not be worn.
The two sandals are identical copies in the same orientation instead of mirrored left and right shoes: same strap curl, same slot placement, same sole outline.

fix: A pair of flip-flops, one left and one right, mirrored. On each, a toe post sits between the first and second toe. From it, two strap arms spread in a V and attach into the opposite side edges of the sole at mid-foot, one on the inner edge and one on the outer edge, leaving an open space for the foot. No strap loops past the sole edge or attaches in the middle of the sole.
